tasks.title: Approve Brazil enterprise risk-management framework
tasks.regulatoryBasis: Res. 520 transition requirements and applicable BCB risk-management framework
tasks.why: The Brazil entity must show an operating framework for material risks including operational, liquidity and other risks relevant to its activities.
actions: Identify the Brazil risk universe and taxonomy.
Set risk appetite, limits, KRIs and escalation triggers.
Document committee/board reporting and breach management.
Map controls and accountable owners to material risks.
tasks.definitionOfDone: Approved framework covers material Brazil risks and is supported by an operating risk register and reporting process.

tasks.title: Internal controls and regulatory compliance monitoring programme
tasks.involved: All control owners; Internal Audit; Board
tasks.why: Policies become evidence only when someone tests whether people actually follow them.
actions: Create Brazil regulatory obligations register.
Map each obligation to control, owner, frequency and evidence.
Create transition compliance monitoring plan.
Define issue severity, remediation, escalation and closure validation.
Run priority pre-filing control tests.
tasks.definitionOfDone: All critical transition obligations have mapped controls, owners and testing evidence; material gaps have dated remediation plans.

tasks.title: Cybersecurity, incident response and continuity controls
tasks.regulatoryBasis: Res. 520 and applicable BCB cybersecurity/cloud requirements
tasks.why: Custody, customer access, APIs and outsourced infrastructure make cyber controls authorization-critical rather than merely ISO decoration.
actions: Map existing ISO 27001 controls to Brazil BCB cyber requirements.
Approve Brazil-applicable cybersecurity policy and accountability.
Validate incident detection, classification, escalation and regulator/customer communications.
Test BCP/DR and critical dependencies for Brazil service flows.
Document privileged access and key/custody security controls.
tasks.definitionOfDone: Brazil cybersecurity and continuity controls are approved, tested and mapped to responsible management.

tasks.title: Relevant-service / cloud outsourcing governance
tasks.involved: CISO; Legal; Compliance; CTO; Vendor owners
tasks.regulatoryBasis: Res. 520 art. 33 and linked BCB outsourcing/cloud requirements
tasks.why: Relevant third parties must be known, contractually controlled and monitorable, including group companies.
actions: Create Brazil relevant-service inventory with location and service description.
Classify materiality/criticality and perform due diligence.
Review contracts for audit, access, security, incident, continuity and termination provisions.
Create ongoing SLA/KRI and annual review process.
Document concentration and exit risks.
tasks.definitionOfDone: Every relevant Brazil service has an approved risk assessment, adequate contract terms and ongoing monitoring owner.

tasks.title: Implement BCB fraud-information sharing requirements
tasks.regulatoryBasis: Res. BCB 343/2023, current version, and linked fraud-sharing regime
tasks.why: The fraud data-sharing controls must be treated as an operational deadline item rather than a paragraph in a fraud policy.
actions: Confirm exact scope and effective-date obligations for Kinetic with Brazilian counsel.
Select/confirm technical mechanism for fraud-data sharing.
Map required data fields, triggers, lawful basis and retention.
Build procedure for identifying, recording and sharing suspected fraud information.
Test production workflow before filing.
tasks.definitionOfDone: Fraud-sharing capability is legally validated, production-ready and tested before the applicable transition deadline.
tasks.risk: Confirm exact VASP transition date/application of the amended fraud-sharing regime in final legal QA.
